user.title: myAmpere
user.description: myAmpere must already be running (e.g. on your Raspberry Pi). How do you want to connect?

reauth_confirm.title: Connect again
reauth_confirm.description: The access was removed in myAmpere or its certificate changed.

pair.title: Pair with myAmpere
pair.description: Enter the address myAmpere runs on. Then Home Assistant and myAmpere show the same 6-digit code, which you confirm in myAmpere.

data_description.host: IP address or name of the device myAmpere runs on, e.g. 192.168.178.20 – without http:// and without :8080.
data_description.port: Default 8443. Only change it if you changed it in myAmpere.

confirm_code.title: Confirm the code
confirm_code.description:
myAmpere reports that the connection was allowed.

**Code: {code}**

Only continue if you just allowed the request from “Home Assistant” in myAmpere (Mehr → Verbundene Apps) and it showed exactly this code. If you did not allow anything there or the code was different, close this window: another device may be answering at this address.

confirm_new_certificate.title: Confirm the code – new certificate
confirm_new_certificate.description:
myAmpere now shows a different certificate than the one Home Assistant knows. That is expected after myAmpere was installed again or moved to another device, otherwise not.

**Code: {code}**

Only continue if you just allowed the request from “Home Assistant” in myAmpere (Mehr → Verbundene Apps) and it showed exactly this code. If in doubt, close this window, create a connection code in myAmpere and choose “Paste a connection code”.

code.title: Paste a connection code
code.description: Create an access in myAmpere under Mehr → Verbundene Apps and paste the connection code here.

data_description.code: Create it in myAmpere under Mehr → Verbundene Apps (More → Connected apps).
data_description.host: Only if Home Assistant reaches myAmpere under a different address than your browser, e.g. the Raspberry Pi's IP address.

hassio_confirm.title: myAmpere app found
hassio_confirm.description: The myAmpere app of this Home Assistant is running. Next, Home Assistant and myAmpere show the same 6-digit code. Confirm it in myAmpere: open it in the sidebar, then More → Connected apps.

error.invalid_code: This is not a valid connection code. Please copy it completely.
error.invalid_auth: The access is invalid or was removed.
error.certificate_mismatch: The certificate does not match the code. Is this really your myAmpere? Otherwise create a new code.
error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach myAmpere. Check the address and the HTTPS port (default 8443).
error.unsupported_version: myAmpere and the integration do not match. Please update both.
error.pairing_failed: myAmpere did not accept the request: {detail}

abort.already_configured: This myAmpere is already set up.
abort.wrong_server: The code belongs to a different myAmpere.
abort.pairing_rejected: The pairing was rejected in myAmpere.
abort.pairing_expired: The request expired (10 minutes). Please start again.
abort.app_connected: myAmpere is connected again, now as the Home Assistant app. Entities and their history stay.

progress.wait_for_approval:
Open myAmpere → Mehr → Verbundene Apps. There is a request from “Home Assistant”.

**Code: {code}**

Only allow the connection if myAmpere shows exactly this code. If it shows a different one, reject it.

data_description.min_interval: 0 = take every value myAmpere sends. Higher values spare small systems such as a Raspberry Pi with an SD card.

confirm.title: Remove the myAmpere integration?
confirm.description: The myAmpere app is no longer installed, so “{title}” has nothing to connect to. Remove the integration with its devices and entities? Their history stays in Home Assistant. If you install the app again, Home Assistant finds it again.
